lessons.title: Airway Assessment & Difficult Airway: Plan A/B/C/D
lessons.summary: คิด airway เป็น continuum ตั้งแต่ basic opening, suction, BVM, SGA, ETT จนถึง rescue airway โดยมี oxygenation เป็นเป้าหมาย ไม่ใช่การ “ต้องใส่ท่อให้ได้”.

sections.title: 1) Airway threat recognition
paragraphs: ดูเสียง/effort/mental status/secretions/blood/facial trauma. Stridor, gurgling, snoring, inability to handle secretions, progressive edema และ severe fatigue เป็น red flags.
bullets: Airway protection ≠ ventilation ≠ oxygenation; ประเมินแยกกัน
GCS อย่างเดียวไม่ควรเป็นข้อบ่งชี้เดี่ยวโดยไม่ดู airway reflex/trajectory/ventilation

sections.title: 2) Difficult airway predictors
paragraphs: LEMON ใช้เตือน difficult laryngoscopy; MOANS ช่วยคิด difficult BVM; RODS ใช้กับ SGA; SMART ใช้คิด surgical airway difficulty. สิ่งเหล่านี้ไม่ใช่ perfect scores แต่เป็น prompts ให้เตรียม backup.

sections.title: 3) Airway strategy
paragraphs: Plan A = optimized first attempt; Plan B = alternate device/SGA; Plan C = oxygenation rescue/BVM; Plan D = emergency front-of-neck accessตาม scope/protocol. ทุกขั้นต้องกำหนด trigger สำหรับ move on เพื่อไม่ fixation error.

sections.title: 4) Pre-intubation checklist
paragraphs: SOAP-ME: suction, oxygen, airway equipment, pharmacy, monitoring, equipment/backup. เพิ่ม hemodynamic optimization, position, preoxygenation and post-intubation plan.

key_points: Suction is a primary airway tool, not an afterthought
red_flags: Rapidly falling mental status with loss of airway protection

quiz.q: Airway success ที่สำคัญที่สุดคืออะไร?
quiz.explain: Airway management is about maintaining oxygenation/ventilation; ETT is one tool.

quiz.q: MOANS ใช้เตือนเรื่องใด?
quiz.explain: MOANS is a common mnemonic for difficult bag-mask ventilation.

lessons.title: Preoxygenation, BVM & Peri-intubation Oxygenation
lessons.summary: ช่วงอันตรายที่สุดของ intubation มักเป็น hypoxemia/hypotension ไม่ใช่แค่ laryngoscopy failure. บทนี้เน้นการสร้าง oxygen reserve, BVM technique และ peri-intubation physiology.

sections.title: 1) Why preoxygenation matters
paragraphs: Preoxygenation replaces nitrogen in functional residual capacity with oxygen to prolong safe apnea time. Patients with shunt physiology, obesity, pregnancy or severe hypoxemia desaturate much faster.

sections.title: 2) BVM technique
paragraphs: Use proper mask size, airway positioning, OPA/NPA when appropriate, two-hand mask seal with second rescuer squeezing bag if available. Watch chest rise and avoid excessive pressure/volume.
bullets: PEEP can help selected hypoxemic patients
Suction before and during ventilation if contaminated

sections.title: 3) Apneic oxygenation & positive pressure
paragraphs: Nasal oxygen during attempts may help selected patients, but does not replace ventilation when ventilation is needed. NIV/CPAP preoxygenation is useful in some severely hypoxemic patients if they can tolerate it and have no contraindication.

sections.title: 4) Hemodynamic preparation
paragraphs: Positive pressure and induction can reduce venous return and BP. Identify shock, optimize volume/vasopressor strategy per protocol, choose induction dose thoughtfully, and monitor closely.

key_points: BVM excellence is a core rescue skill
Avoid both hypoxia and excessive ventilation

research_updates.title: Bag-mask ventilation during intubation
research_updates.takeaway: A randomized trial in critically ill adults found bag-mask ventilation during the apneic period reduced severe hypoxemia without a clear increase in aspiration; application depends on aspiration risk and local airway practice.

research_updates.title: PREOXI: NIV preoxygenation reduced hypoxemia
research_updates.takeaway: In 1301 critically ill adults, preoxygenation with noninvasive ventilation reduced hypoxemia during intubation compared with an oxygen mask (9.1% vs 18.5%). Apply to appropriate patients with trained teams and aspiration/pressure considerations.

quiz.q: ผู้ป่วย severe hypoxemia ก่อน intubation ควรคิดอะไร?
quiz.explain: Optimization before laryngoscopy reduces peri-intubation hypoxemia risk.

lessons.title: RSI / Tracheal Intubation: First-pass success, drugs, capnography
lessons.summary: RSI คือ controlled process: prepare → preoxygenate → optimize physiology → induce/paralyze → place → confirm → secure → post-intubation sedation/ventilation.

sections.title: 1) Indications & decision
paragraphs: Intubate when airway cannot be protected, oxygenation/ventilation cannot be maintained, anticipated deterioration requires definitive airway, or procedural need justifies risk. Avoid reflex intubation without considering BVM/SGA/NIV alternatives.

sections.title: 2) First-pass strategy
paragraphs: First-pass success matters because repeated attempts increase hypoxemia, aspiration and trauma. Optimize operator/device/position/bougie/suction before starting.

sections.title: 3) Video vs direct laryngoscopy
paragraphs: DEVICE trial in critically ill adults showed higher first-attempt success with video laryngoscopy (85.1% vs 70.8%) without reduction in severe complication rate, supporting VL when equipment/training are available.
bullets: VL does not eliminate need for DL skills
Screen view can be excellent while tube delivery remains difficult—optimize stylet/bougie technique

sections.title: 4) Confirmation
paragraphs: Continuous waveform capnography + clinical assessment is the most reliable confirmation/monitoring method in adult arrest. Reconfirm after movement and if waveform/ventilation changes.

sections.title: 5) Post-intubation care
paragraphs: Tube fixation, analgesia/sedation, ventilator/BVM settings, BP monitoring, EtCO₂ trend and repeat auscultation are part of the procedure—not optional afterthoughts.

key_points: First attempt should be best attempt
Do not let intubation interrupt CPR excessively
quick_review: VL improves first-pass success in DEVICE trial

research_updates.title: DEVICE randomized trial
research_updates.takeaway: Video laryngoscopy improved first-attempt intubation success from 70.8% to 85.1% in critically ill adults; severe complications were similar.

research_updates.title: DEVICE randomized trial: video vs direct laryngoscopy
research_updates.takeaway: Among critically ill adults in the DEVICE trial, first-attempt success was 85.1% with video laryngoscopy vs 70.8% with direct laryngoscopy; severe complications were similar. This supports VL availability/training but does not remove the need for airway planning and rescue skills.

research_updates.title: PREOXI: preoxygenation is an active intervention
research_updates.takeaway: PREOXI strengthens evidence that positive-pressure NIV preoxygenation can reduce peri-intubation hypoxemia in critically ill adults; device choice should be individualized.

quiz.explain: First-attempt success was higher with video laryngoscopy.

quiz.q: Most reliable ETT confirmation adjunct in adult arrest?
quiz.explain: AHA recommends continuous waveform capnography in addition to clinical assessment.

lessons.title: Acute Respiratory Failure: Asthma, COPD, Pulmonary Edema, Pneumonia
lessons.summary: เรียนแบบ physiology-first: oxygenation failure, ventilation failure, work of breathing และ impending fatigue แล้วค่อยแยกโรค.

sections.title: 1) Respiratory failure framework
paragraphs: Type 1 = hypoxemic failure; Type 2 = hypercapnic/ventilatory failure. ผู้ป่วยอาจมีทั้งสอง. ดู mental status, respiratory effort, speech, air entry, SpO₂ และ capnography/ABG when available.
bullets: Silent chest + fatigue = late ominous sign
Normal SpO₂ ไม่ได้ยืนยัน ventilation ปกติ
Rising CO₂ + declining effort can indicate fatigue

sections.title: 2) Asthma/COPD
paragraphs: Bronchospasm causes expiratory flow limitation and dynamic hyperinflation. Prioritize bronchodilation, oxygen to target, steroids per protocol and avoid excessive ventilation if mechanically ventilating severe obstruction.
bullets: A suddenly quiet chest can mean worsening obstruction, not improvement

sections.title: 3) Cardiogenic pulmonary edema
paragraphs: Acute pulmonary edema is a pressure/volume problem causing alveolar flooding and severe work of breathing. CPAP/NIV can improve oxygenation and reduce preload/afterload in appropriate conscious patients; nitrates/other therapy depend on BP/local protocol.

sections.title: 4) Pneumonia/other parenchymal disease
paragraphs: Shunt physiology may make simple oxygen less effective; positioning, high-flow/NIV or intubation may be required depending on trajectory and resources.

key_points: Assess work of breathing, not SpO₂ alone
Ventilation failure can exist with acceptable saturation
NIV is powerful but requires cooperation and airway protection
quick_review: Pulmonary edema: think CPAP/NIV if appropriate

quiz.q: SpO₂ 98% แต่ผู้ป่วยซึมและ hypoventilate สามารถมี respiratory failure ได้หรือไม่?
quiz.explain: SpO₂ reflects oxygenation, not ventilation/CO₂ clearance.

lessons.title: Acute Asthma 2026: Bronchospasm, Dynamic Hyperinflation & Escalation
lessons.summary: ตั้งแต่ airway inflammation/bronchospasm ไปถึง silent chest, auto-PEEP และ peri-intubation collapse.

sections.title: 1) Pathophysiology
paragraphs: Asthma combines variable bronchoconstriction, airway inflammation/edema and mucus. Severe obstruction prolongs expiration; incomplete exhalation produces dynamic hyperinflation and intrinsic PEEP, increasing work of breathing and impairing venous return.

sections.title: 2) Severity is clinical
paragraphs: Speech, posture, accessory muscle use, mental state, air entry, RR/HR and oxygenation matter. A “quiet” or silent chest in a tiring patient can mean critically low airflow rather than improvement.

sections.title: 3) Initial treatment principles
paragraphs: Repeated inhaled bronchodilator, systemic corticosteroid and oxygen titrated to clinical need form the core; add adjuncts/escalation for severe or refractory disease according to protocol. Treat anaphylaxis differently when systemic allergic features are present.

sections.title: 4) Ventilation/intubation
paragraphs: Intubation is high risk because positive pressure can worsen hyperinflation and hypotension. If ventilated, allow long expiratory time, avoid excessive minute ventilation and watch for auto-PEEP/barotrauma. Permissive hypercapnia may be accepted in selected patients under appropriate care.

sections.title: 5) Differential
paragraphs: Anaphylaxis, COPD, pulmonary edema, PE, pneumothorax, foreign body, upper airway obstruction and vocal cord dysfunction can mimic wheeze.

prehospital_focus: Prepare escalation early in near-fatal asthma
red_flags: Rising/normalizing CO₂ in a tiring patient

research_updates.title: GINA 2026 Strategy Report
research_updates.takeaway: GINA 2026 integrates newly reviewed evidence and remains a current global asthma strategy source. Use local acute-care protocol for drug concentrations and EMS scope.

lessons.title: COPD Exacerbation 2026: Oxygen, Ventilation & Hypercapnia
lessons.summary: ประเมิน exacerbation, gas-exchange failure, oxygen titration และบทบาท NIV.

sections.title: 1) What worsens COPD
paragraphs: Infection, air pollution, heart failure, PE, pneumothorax, arrhythmia and medication issues may trigger or mimic exacerbation.

sections.title: 2) Gas exchange
paragraphs: V/Q mismatch drives hypoxemia; severe obstruction and fatigue can produce hypercapnic respiratory failure. Oxygen should treat hypoxemia but excessive uncontrolled oxygen can worsen hypercapnia in susceptible patients through V/Q and Haldane effects.

sections.title: 3) NIV
paragraphs: NIV is a key escalation for appropriate patients with acute hypercapnic respiratory failure who can protect the airway and cooperate. Monitor work of breathing, mental state, gas exchange and failure signs.

sections.title: 4) Failure signs
paragraphs: Worsening acidosis/hypercapnia, exhaustion, inability to protect airway, refractory hypoxemia, shock or intolerance should trigger escalation and intubation consideration.

research_updates.title: GOLD 2026 Report
research_updates.takeaway: The 2026 GOLD report is the current evidence-based global COPD strategy; local acute-exacerbation pathways should determine exact therapies and targets.

lessons.title: Mechanical Ventilation Basics for Paramedics: Settings, Waveforms & DOPE
lessons.summary: เข้าใจ ventilator แบบ physiology-first: oxygenation, ventilation, pressure, synchrony และ troubleshooting.

sections.title: 1) Four questions
paragraphs: What mode? What tidal volume/minute ventilation? What oxygenation strategy (FiO₂/PEEP)? Is the patient synchronized and safe? Settings must reflect predicted body weight and disease physiology, not simply actual weight.

sections.title: 2) Oxygenation vs ventilation
paragraphs: Oxygenation is mainly influenced by FiO₂, PEEP and lung recruitment; CO₂ removal is primarily related to alveolar minute ventilation. Changes have hemodynamic and barotrauma consequences.

sections.title: 3) Pressures
paragraphs: Peak pressure reflects airway resistance + elastic load; plateau pressure better reflects alveolar/static pressure when measured correctly. Rising peak with stable plateau suggests resistance; both rising can imply compliance loss.

sections.title: 4) DOPE sudden deterioration
paragraphs: Displacement, Obstruction, Pneumothorax, Equipment failure. Disconnect and hand-ventilate when appropriate while rapidly evaluating the patient and circuit.

sections.title: 5) Disease-specific thinking
paragraphs: Asthma/COPD need expiratory time; ARDS prioritizes lung-protective strategy; severe shock may worsen with high intrathoracic pressure.

prehospital_focus: Monitor pressure alarms and hemodynamics after every setting change
pitfalls: Using actual weight rather than predicted body weight for lung-protective VT

sources.label: OneDrive Ventilator OSCE — local teaching source

lessons.title: Pulmonary Embolism: From Dyspnea to Obstructive Shock
lessons.summary: คิด PE เมื่อ dyspnea/chest pain/syncope ไม่มีคำอธิบาย โดยเฉพาะมี VTE risk และ RV strain.

sections.title: 1) Physiology
paragraphs: Pulmonary vascular obstruction raises RV afterload → RV dilation/ischemia → septal shift → reduced LV preload and shock. Hypoxemia often results from V/Q mismatch.

sections.title: 2) Presentation
paragraphs: Dyspnea, pleuritic pain, tachycardia, syncope, hypoxemia, hemoptysis or shock; massive/high-risk PE can present as PEA arrest.

sections.title: 3) Risk context
paragraphs: Recent surgery/immobility, active cancer, prior VTE, pregnancy/postpartum and estrogen exposure increase probability, but PE can occur without obvious risk.

sections.title: 4) Prehospital priorities
paragraphs: Support oxygenation/ventilation and perfusion, avoid unnecessary delays, obtain ECG when useful and alert receiving facility when high-risk PE/obstructive shock is suspected.

lessons.title: Pneumothorax & Tension Physiology
lessons.summary: อย่ารอภาพถ่ายเมื่อ obstructive shock + compatible chest findings บอก tension pneumothorax.

sections.title: 1) Simple vs tension
paragraphs: Air in pleural space causes lung collapse. Tension physiology occurs when rising intrathoracic pressure impairs venous return and cardiac output; it is a physiologic diagnosis, not merely “large pneumothorax.”

sections.title: 2) Findings
paragraphs: Acute dyspnea/chest pain, asymmetric breath sounds, increasing ventilatory pressure, subcutaneous emphysema. In tension: hypotension, severe distress, JVD may occur; tracheal deviation is late/inconsistent.

sections.title: 3) Ventilated patients
paragraphs: Positive pressure can convert a pneumothorax into tension rapidly. Sudden desaturation, hypotension and high airway pressure should trigger DOPE evaluation.

sections.title: 4) Management
paragraphs: Immediate decompression is indicated for tension physiology according to local protocol; definitive chest drainage follows. Technique/location/device must match training and system protocol.

lessons.title: Acute Pulmonary Edema: CPAP/NIV, Afterload & the Failing LV
lessons.summary: เข้าใจว่าบางราย “น้ำท่วมปอด” เกิดจาก abrupt pressure redistribution มากกว่าปริมาณน้ำส่วนเกินอย่างเดียว.

sections.title: 1) Hemodynamics
paragraphs: High LV filling pressure transmits backward into pulmonary capillaries. In hypertensive sympathetic crashing acute pulmonary edema, extreme afterload can rapidly drive fluid into alveoli.

sections.title: 2) Recognition
paragraphs: Severe dyspnea, orthopnea, diffuse crackles, diaphoresis, hypertension or hypotension, frothy sputum in advanced cases. Consider ACS, arrhythmia, renal failure and valvular disease.

sections.title: 3) Noninvasive positive pressure
paragraphs: CPAP/NIV can improve oxygenation, reduce work of breathing and alter preload/afterload favorably in appropriate patients; avoid in inability to protect airway, vomiting, severe agitation or profound instability without a plan.

sections.title: 4) BP phenotype matters
paragraphs: Hypertensive patients may benefit from vasodilator-focused management under protocol; cardiogenic shock is a different physiology and should not be treated identically.
